findings.title: stringifyPath emits unparseable path for integer-valued numbers >= 1e21
findings.property: for any finite number segment, parsePath(stringifyPath(segs)) does not throw (stringifyPath returns 'a string path that can be used with other dot-prop functions')
findings.property_test: stringify of any finite number segment is parseable
findings.expected: a path string that parsePath accepts (e.g. the number treated as a string key like '1e\+21'/escaped, or a digit-only index)
findings.actual: returns '[1e+21]', and parsePath('[1e+21]') throws "Invalid character 'e' in an index at position 3"
findings.evidence: readme: stringifyPath 'Returns a string path that can be used with other dot-prop functions'; type is Array<string | number>. Number.isInteger(1e21) is true so formatPathSegment uses `[${segment}]`, which stringifies in exponent notation.

error.message:
Got unwanted exception: stringifyPath([1e21]) gave unparseable "[1e+21]"
Actual message: "Invalid character 'e' in an index at position 3"

review.title: stringifyPath emits an unparseable index like "[1e+21]" for integer numbers >= 1e21
review.reason: formatPathSegment sends every non-negative integer to bracket notation via `[${segment}]`. For values >= 1e21, `String(n)` switches to exponent notation, so the output contains 'e' and '+', and parsePath rejects it. The function already sends non-integers and negatives down the escaped-string-key path precisely so the output stays parseable, so this case is an overlooked edge of the same rule. A maintainer would likely accept a small fix, such as treating numbers whose string form is not all digits as string keys. The input is an extreme edge case, so severity is low.

fix.reason: the repro passes on the patched code
